_note: Starter advice written from general extension guidance. Before the demo, Teammate 4 should check each card against a .edu or USDA extension page and fill in source.

tomato_healthy.name: Looks healthy
tomato_healthy.signs: Even green color, no spots or curling.
do_now: Keep checking the lower leaves once a week.
prevent: Water at the base in the morning.
Mulch so soil doesn't splash onto leaves.
tomato_healthy.call_expert_if: New spots appear and spread within a few days.

tomato_early_blight.name: Early blight
tomato_early_blight.signs: Brown spots with rings like a target, usually on older, lower leaves first.
do_now: Remove spotted lower leaves and bag them.
Wash hands and tools before touching healthy plants.
prevent: Mulch around plants to stop soil splash.
Rotate tomatoes and potatoes to a new spot next year.
tomato_early_blight.call_expert_if: Spots reach the upper half of the plant or the fruit.

tomato_late_blight.name: Late blight
tomato_late_blight.signs: Dark, greasy-looking patches that spread fast; white fuzz underneath in damp weather.
do_now: Remove and bag affected plants. Don't compost them.
Check nearby tomato and potato plants today.
prevent: Water at the base, not the leaves.
Space plants so leaves dry quickly.
tomato_late_blight.call_expert_if: It is on more than a few plants. Late blight spreads to neighbors' fields, so report it.

potato_healthy.name: Looks healthy
potato_healthy.signs: Even green leaves, no dark patches.
do_now: Keep scouting weekly, more often in wet weather.
potato_healthy.call_expert_if: Dark patches appear after rainy days.

potato_early_blight.name: Early blight
potato_early_blight.signs: Small brown spots with target-like rings on older leaves.
do_now: Remove the worst leaves and bag them.
Keep plants watered evenly; stressed plants get it worse.
prevent: Rotate away from potatoes and tomatoes for 2-3 years.
potato_early_blight.call_expert_if: More than a third of the leaves are spotted.

potato_late_blight.name: Late blight
potato_late_blight.signs: Large dark, wet-looking patches, often with a pale edge; can rot tubers.
do_now: Remove and bag infected plants right away.
Don't dig tubers from infected rows in wet weather.
prevent: Destroy cull piles and volunteer potatoes.
potato_late_blight.call_expert_if: You see it at all. Contact your extension office the same day.

pepper_healthy.name: Looks healthy
do_now: Keep checking leaves after storms.
prevent: Avoid working in plants while leaves are wet.
pepper_healthy.call_expert_if: Small dark spots appear on many leaves.

pepper_bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial spot
pepper_bacterial_spot.signs: Small dark, water-soaked spots that turn brown; leaves may yellow and drop.
do_now: Remove badly spotted leaves.
Stay out of the rows while plants are wet.
prevent: Rotate peppers and tomatoes to new ground.
Buy certified clean seed and transplants.
pepper_bacterial_spot.call_expert_if: Leaves are dropping or spots appear on fruit.

crusting.name: Surface crust
crusting.what_it_means: A hard skin on top stops seedlings and water getting through.
do_now: Break the crust lightly with a rake before planting.
fix_long_term: Add compost or mulch to the surface.

compaction.name: Compacted soil
compaction.what_it_means: Packed soil holds less air and water, so roots stay shallow.
do_now: Keep equipment and foot traffic off wet ground.

erosion.name: Erosion
erosion.what_it_means: Topsoil, the most fertile layer, is washing or blowing away.
do_now: Cover bare soil with mulch or residue.
fix_long_term: Plant across slopes, not up and down.

salt_crust.name: Salt buildup
salt_crust.what_it_means: White crust can mean salts that burn roots and block water uptake.
do_now: Get a lab soil test to confirm before acting.

waterlogging.name: Waterlogged
waterlogging.what_it_means: Standing water drowns roots and invites root rot.
do_now: Stay off the field until it drains.
fix_long_term: Use raised beds or drainage ditches.
Add organic matter to improve structure.

cracking_dry.name: Dry and cracked
cracking_dry.what_it_means: Clay soils shrink and crack when very dry; roots can tear.
do_now: Water deeply and less often rather than a little every day.
fix_long_term: Add compost to improve water holding.

low_organic_matter.name: Low organic matter
low_organic_matter.what_it_means: Pale soil often has little organic matter, so it holds less water and nutrients.
do_now: Leave crop residue on the field instead of removing it.

ph_low.name: Acidic soil (low pH)
ph_low.what_it_means: Most vegetables do best around pH 6 to 7. Low pH locks up nutrients.
do_now: Confirm with a lab soil test before adding lime.
fix_long_term: Lime based on the lab's recommendation, not a guess.

ph_high.name: Alkaline soil (high pH)
ph_high.what_it_means: High pH can cause iron and other nutrient shortages; leaves may yellow.
do_now: Confirm with a lab soil test.
fix_long_term: Follow the lab's recommendation for amendments.
